title: Synthwave
summary: Neon grids, striped sunsets, and chrome lettering on a black night sky. The 1980s remembered as a movie.
lede: The visual side of the synthwave music microgenre of the late 2000s and 2010s, usually called the Outrun aesthetic after the 1986 Sega game *Out Run*: a dark night sky, a striped retrosun on the horizon, a glowing magenta laser grid that recedes to a vanishing point, chrome and airbrush-script logotypes, and 1980s sports cars and palm trees, in magenta, cyan, and violet. Wikipedia describes outrun as a term for “retro 1980s aesthetics such as VHS tracking artefacts, magenta neon, and gridlines”. Unlike [vaporwave](style:vaporwave), it celebrates its sources without irony and keeps a polished, high-contrast finish.

era.note: Kavinsky’s “Testarossa Autodrive” (2006) and the Valerie Collective set the template, per the Aesthetics Wiki; Wikidata dates the genre to 2005. Drive (2011), Hotline Miami (2012), Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon (2013), and Kung Fury (2015) spread the look. It continues in the 2020s in games, merchandise, and music videos.

attestation.label: PC Gamer (Phil Iwaniuk, 4 October 2017): How synthwave music inspired games to explore a past that never existed

lineage.label: Out Run (1986 video game)
lineage.note: Wikipedia: the term “outrun” comes from the 1986 Sega arcade racing game. PC Gamer notes that the Ferrari Testarossa and palm trees on Kavinsky’s *OutRun* album cover (2013) reference the game.

lineage.label: Tron (1982 film)
lineage.note: PC Gamer: in synthwave games “Tron’s neon lines often appear”. The glowing wireframe grid floor descends from its vector graphics.

lineage.label: Blade Runner (1982 film)
lineage.note: Wikipedia names *Blade Runner*, “both the soundtrack and the film itself”, as a key reference point. PC Gamer: “Blade Runner’s cityscapes” recur in synthwave game art.

lineage.label: Miami Vice
lineage.note: Invisible Oranges, quoted by Wikipedia, describes the genre’s bright side as “Miami Vice vibes”: pastel-neon coastal nights, sports cars, and palm silhouettes.

lineage.label: Italo disco
lineage.note: The Aesthetics Wiki lists Italo disco as a predecessor and compares synthwave’s airbrushed chrome script lettering to Italo disco album covers.

Wikipedia: Nicholas Diak traces both genres to the same shift toward 1980s homage after *Grand Theft Auto: Vice City* (2002), and calls “retrowave” an umbrella that covers both. The Aesthetics Wiki tabulates the difference: synthwave is earnest, dark, and high-contrast; vaporwave is ironic, pastel, and lo-fi.

lineage.label: Darksynth
lineage.note: Wikidata classes darksynth as a subclass of synthwave. The Aesthetics Wiki: it swaps the neon-sunset palette for red and black, occult imagery, and horror tropes. This record covers the Outrun core, not that branch.
The Aesthetics Wiki lists cyberpunk as a related aesthetic, and Wikipedia’s synthwave article links it. Both use neon on black; cyberpunk is dystopian and urban, synthwave nostalgic and open-horizon.

grammar.text: Deep black, navy, and violet grounds carry magenta, cyan, and violet light. The sun adds yellow and orange. Colors glow rather than fill.
A flat plane, usually a laser grid, recedes to a central vanishing point under a striped sun or a skyline. Compositions are symmetrical and centered on the horizon.

Heavy italic capitals rendered as chrome, with a sky-blue top, a hard horizon line, and a pink reflection below, often paired with a glowing airbrush or brush script. Secondary text is wide, spaced techno capitals.
The striped retrosun, the wireframe grid, wireframe mountains, 1980s supercars such as the Testarossa, Countach, and DeLorean, palm silhouettes, and night city skylines.
Neon tube glows, chrome highlights, star fields, and lens flares. The finish is clean and high-definition. VHS scan lines appear as an accent, not as decay.
Panels and buttons are dark, square boxes outlined with a thin glowing line, like a neon sign or a vector display.
The grid scrolls toward the viewer, the sun sinks, and the road runs on in loops, as in music videos and arcade attract modes.

synthesis: Provisional: no references are recorded yet. The record is written from the sources in the attestation list. The Outrun core is consistent across them: a striped sun, a magenta laser grid, chrome lettering, and cars and palms on a night sky.

diagnostic: A dark night-sky ground with magenta, cyan, and violet neon light.
A striped sun on a horizon, a glowing perspective grid floor, or both.
Chrome or glowing italic lettering, often with a neon script word.
1980s supercars, palm silhouettes, wireframe mountains, or night skylines, shown without irony.
counter: A pastel or faded palette, classical statues, Windows 95 windows, or glitch decay as the main surface: that is vaporwave.
Rain, grime, crowded street signage, and a dystopian city mood without a horizon or a sunset: that is cyberpunk.
Red and black only, with occult or horror imagery: that is the darksynth branch.
Light or white grounds with neon used only as small accents.

confusions.difference: Both use a grid floor and a striped sun. Synthwave is dark, saturated, polished, and sincere, with chrome type, cars, and palms. Vaporwave is pastel, faded, glitched, and ironic, with statues, Windows 95 chrome, and fullwidth or Japanese text.

Cyberpunk is a dystopian city at street level: rain, dense signs, grime, and hacker interfaces in neon on black. Synthwave looks at an open horizon at sunset, with a clean grid, chrome logos, and nostalgia instead of dread.
Y2K uses silver chrome, iridescent blobs, rounded plastic, and light grounds. Synthwave chrome is a striped 1980s logotype on a black sky with neon grids, and its corners are square.
Darksynth is a branch of synthwave that drops the sunset palette for red, black, and horror imagery. Count it as related, not as the core.

do: Use a near-black navy-to-violet sky gradient as the page background, warming toward magenta at the horizon.
Put a striped sun on the horizon of the hero and a receding magenta laser grid below it.
Set display headings in heavy italic capitals with a chrome gradient: light top, hard horizon line at the middle, pink reflection below.
Outline panels and buttons with a 1 px neon line and a centered, blurred glow. Keep the corners square.
Use magenta and cyan as the two neon colors, and yellow-orange only for the sun and for figures such as prices.
Keep body text light on the dark part of the sky or on a dark translucent panel.
dont: Do not use pastel or faded colors as the base. That reads as vaporwave.
Do not add glitch decay, Windows 95 windows, or classical statues.
Do not use offset or hard drop shadows. Neon glows are centered and blurred.
Do not put body text on the sun, the grid, or the bright horizon band.
Do not set long text in script or chrome type. Keep them for one or two words.
Do not animate the grid or flicker the neon for users who prefer reduced motion.
avoid: Finance, health, government, and other products where calm and trust come first. The style is loud and theatrical.
Long reading and dense documentation. Glow and dark grounds tire the eye over long text.
Daylight, outdoor, or nature brands. The style is nocturnal and artificial.

tokens.$description: Authored tokens for synthwave. Shorthand values; tools/build.mjs writes DTCG 2025.10.

primary.$description: Neon magenta: grid lines, borders, glows.

secondary.$description: Neon cyan: the second tube color.

horizon.$description: Sky color just above the horizon.

panel.$description: Panel fill at 70% opacity: the sky shows through.

mono.$description: Wide techno caps for labels. Not a monospace face; synthwave labels are not terminal text.

script.$description: Airbrush-style script for a second word under the chrome logotype.

sm.$description: Neon tube glow: centered, blurred, no offset.

md.$description: Panel glow with a tight core and a wide halo.

sky.$description: Night sky that warms toward the horizon.

sun.$description: Retrosun: yellow at the top, magenta at the horizon.

chrome.$description: Chrome lettering: sky reflection, a hard horizon line, then a pink ground reflection.

references.title: Vaporwave wallpaper (Mike Grauer Jr)
references.note: Partial fit: the striped sun over a magenta grid plain is the core synthwave scene, but the violet sky is softer than its usual black night.

references.title: Chase The Sun (G. Casqueiro)
references.note: The Outrun landscape in motion: a glowing wireframe floor and peaks that lead to a sun on the horizon, under a violet and magenta sky.

references.title: Drive (2011 film), US theatrical poster
references.note: Partial fit: the film is a named source of the synthwave revival and its hot-pink script title became a template, but this poster is light and photographic, with no neon, grid, or night sky.

references.title: Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon
references.note: Partial fit: the game made the neon-and-VHS 1980s look mainstream, and its key art is by a leading synthwave cover artist, but the screenshots show interiors, not the sunset-and-grid scene.

references.title: FM-84, Atlas (album cover)
references.note: The retrosun alone: a striped yellow-to-magenta disc on a navy starry sky, which is the motif in its most reduced, iconic form.

references.title: GUNSHIP, GUNSHIP (album cover)
references.note: Every Outrun motif in one frame: a striped sun, a receding laser grid, a glowing wireframe mountain, a star field, and a brushed logotype.

references.title: Hotline Miami
references.note: Partial fit: one of the works that spread the synthwave sound and its pink-violet night palette, palms, and 1980s Miami setting, but in pixel art and without the grid and sun.

references.title: Kavinsky, OutRun (album cover)
references.note: The album that named the Outrun look after the 1986 Sega game: a Testarossa, palms, a night sky, and a neon brush-script logotype.

references.title: Kung Fury (2015 film), Cannes poster
references.note: Partial fit: the film is a named landmark of the style and the poster has the sun, lightning, palms, Countach, and a red-and-blue offset brush title, but it is a warm painted montage, not a neon-on-black scene.

references.title: Synthwave banner (j4p4n, Openclipart)
references.note: The author made it as a banner for the genre’s aesthetic: a striped sun, a glowing magenta grid, and a neon script word on a dark ground.

references.title: The Midnight live at Brixton Academy, 2022
references.note: Partial fit: it documents how a leading synthwave band stages itself, in magenta, violet, and blue light with neon-like horizontal bars, but it is a concert photograph, not designed graphics.

references.title: The Midnight, Endless Summer (album cover)
references.note: A neon-tube script logotype, a black ground, and VHS tracking lines used as a nostalgic accent: the type and surface side of the style.
